answer: Proof-of-Stake protocols mitigate Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock capital as collateral. An attacker attempting to spawn a raven swarm of nodes must acquire the majority of tokens, an economic delta that renders mass identity forgery prohibitively expensive. Unlike a whisper campaign to inflate influence, true voting power is tied to staked assets, ensuring that each malicious identity incurs a tangible financial cost that scales linearly with the network size, effectively preventing cheap replication.
